title: Transport of invertibility to the non-iterated fibre product
statement: Let f:X→S, j:W→S, h:T→W be scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme] and M an O_X-module. Let β_M be the canonical non-iterated direct-image map constructed in [lem-sc-picard-canonical-base-change-comparisons]. If the canonical cartesian base-change map for p_W:X_W→W and h, applied to q_W^*M, is invertible [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-map-open-restriction], then β_M is invertible. No rank or flatness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Canonical base-change construction, with pullback composition from Tags 0096 and 0097 and full inverse-image isomorphic open squares from Tag 00A0.

proof.text: For a square and an isomorphism e of its top-right object, apply the open-square isomorphism theorem to the square with top e and bottom the identity. Its full inverse-image hypothesis holds because e is surjective. Paste it to the original square. If the original base-change map is invertible, every factor in the pasting formula is invertible, and so is the outer base-change map.

Paste the pullback squares defining X_W and its further pullback along h. The inverse of the resulting isoPullback is e:X_T≅X_W×_W T. Its second projection is p_T. Its first projection equals the explicit v by pullback.hom_ext and the two projection identities. Apply the first step to transport invertibility to the square with top v. Compose with pushforward of the explicit tensor-composition and equality isomorphisms, which are invertible.
